 JOHANNESBURG, South Africa (AP) — Ryan Rickelton's century helped South Africa take a commanding 157-run lead on first innings on Day 4 of the first cricket test against Bangladesh at the Wanderers on Wednesday.
 Rickelton’s knock of 102, combined with half-centuries from Kagiso Rabada and skipper Temba Bavuma, saw the Proteas bowled out for 557 at lunch in reply to Bangladesh's total of 400.
 Other WRAL Top Stories
 Rabada scored 72, with 10 fours and two sixes, and put on 117 with Rickelton for the eighth wicket. It was his second test half century.
 Bavuma, who had to retire hurt the previous day, returned to make 68 not out. Despite being hampered in movement, he put on 45 for the 10th wicket with Dane Paterson (29).
 Rickelton reached his fourth test hundred off 159 balls. Overall, he faced 165 balls and hit 13 fours before being stumped off Mehidy Hasan Miraz.
 In between, Miraz had Rabada stumped. Hasan Mahmud bowled Paterson on the stroke of lunch, but it was a no ball and the session was extended by 30 minutes on account of the final wicket remaining.
 Ebadot Hossain finally removed Paterson to end the innings. The hosts scored 171 runs in the morning session.
